note: Which local model to run on which machine. Shares its shape with hardware-db.json so both go through the same submission path: a top-level format block, then entries, each with an id, what it needs, and how confident we are. Add a row by opening a pull request; say what machine you ran it on and what you measured. `confirmed` means somebody ran it on that hardware and it worked. `known` means it should fit and nobody here has proved it.

profiles.note: The hardware profile comes from `xos hardware`. It decides which entries are even candidates, because promising a model a machine cannot hold produces a bad first hour.
profiles.on_thresholds: Minimums are written against what a machine actually reports, not what it was sold as. A machine sold as 8GB reports something near 7800 MB, because firmware and an integrated GPU take their cut before Linux sees any of it. A threshold of 8192 there would exclude every 8GB machine, which is the machine XOS exists for.
profiles.local: a GPU with at least 4GB of VRAM
profiles.cpu: no usable GPU, but enough memory to run something small slowly
profiles.api-only: neither, so no local model is pulled at all

entries.name: Gemma 4 E4B
entries.why: The reference model. Confirmed working on a GTX 1080 through both Ollama and LM Studio, which is the machine XOS is built around. Tool-call reliability is what P1 measures, and this is what it was measured against.

entries.name: Qwen3 8B
entries.why: Stronger at tool calls than its size suggests, but it wants the whole of an 8GB card, which leaves nothing for the desktop on a machine where the same GPU drives the display.

entries.name: Llama 3.2 3B
entries.why: The fallback for a smaller card, and the best of the CPU-only options. It escalates more often than Gemma, which costs API money, but it runs where Gemma does not.

entries.name: Qwen3 1.7B
entries.why: For a machine with no usable GPU at all. Slow, and it escalates often, but it means the reflex layer exists rather than every single request going to an API.
